items.title: Assam to restrict construction in flood-prone areas under proposed zoning law: CM
points: The Assam government plans to bring the floodplains of the Brahmaputra and Barak river basins under a legal land-use zoning system to restrict and regulate construction in vulnerable areas, Chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said on Sunday.
The move aims to address the risks posed by unregulated development in flood-prone areas.
The state government has prepared the Assam Flood Plain Zoning Bill, 2026, which will be tabled during the winter session of the state assembly next month.

The proposed zoning system would add a land-use regulation mechanism to the state’s existing flood-control measures, which include embankments, riverbank protection, river-training works and drainage improvements.
The Assam State Disaster Management Plan, 2022, called for a regulatory framework to demarcate vulnerable areas and manage construction in floodplains.
During a review of the draft on November 5, Sarma directed officials to ensure that lawful existing property owners were protected.
The proposed framework provides for a 60-day period for public hearings and objections, as well as online and physical mechanisms to appeal against zoning decisions.

points: Anakapalli district police have invoked Prevention of Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (PIT NDPS) Act, 1988, against three habitual ganja smugglers, with a history of repeated involvement in narcotics cases.

items.title: History must go beyond kings and dynasties, says UoH history professor
points: History professor at the University of Hyderabad, Bhangya Bhukya has called for a more inclusive approach to Indian historiography and emphasised the need to give due recognition to the histories of south India, marginalised communities and local populations.
Mr. Bhukya was delivering the keynote address at the 45th South Indian History Congress (SIHC), held at Mahatma Gandhi University, Nalgonda.

He called for comprehensive research into the political, economic, social and cultural developments of south India between the 6th and 12th centuries, with particular attention to dynasties such as the Pallavas, Cholas and Kakatiyas.

He further emphasised that historical research should extend beyond kings, dynasties and wars to explore maritime trade, merchant guilds, international relations and the contributions of merchants, artisans, sculptors and labour communities.
He also highlighted the importance of Jain and Buddhist literature and Jataka tales as valuable sources for understanding the lives, occupations and social relationships of ordinary people.

points: Ahead of next year's Assembly elections, Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh on Sunday formed a four-member committee to oversee and coordinate the induction of leaders from other parties.

The accused have been booked under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) as well as the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, for allegedly hurling caste-based slurs at the victim’s family, the police added.
According to the police, the two families live about 200 metres away from each other.
The incident took place when the deceased – Puja Kumar – was visiting her parent’s house in Loni Border’s Indirapuri.
“At around 10pm, Puja’s brother Aman Kumar urinated near the accused’s house.
She was rushed to a local hospital in Delhi where she was declared dead,” Ghaziabad Deputy Commissioner of Police (rural zone) Surendra Nath Tiwari told HT.

points: The Government Railway Police (GRP) and Railway Protection Force (RPF) swung into action on Saturday evening after receiving a call alleging a bomb threat to the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT), which turned out to be a hoax, officials said.
A call was received by the control room at Wadi Bunder received a call at 6:40 p.m. on Saturday, with the caller claiming a bomb had been planted at the station.

An RPF dog squad was also deployed to search the premises, including suburban and long-distance platforms, foot overbridges and the parcel area, he said.
The Bomb Detection and Disposal Squad extensively searched the busy railway terminus’ premises but found nothing suspicious there, officials said.
Officials added that no suspicious person, explosive material or unclaimed object was found on the station premises or inside any train.

items.title: Six arrested as Delhi Police busts family-run heroin trafficking network, seizes drugs worth ₹5 crore
points: Delhi Police on Sunday said it has busted a "family-run" interstate heroin trafficking network, arresting six persons and seizing 2.25 kg of the contraband worth around ₹5 crore.

The operation began on September 11 following a tip-off that a man, identified as Rohit Divakar, his wife and brother were transporting heroin on two-wheelers from Signature Bridge towards Khajuri Khas.
The three were intercepted on Wazirabad Road, and more than 2 kg of heroin was recovered from a backpack on Vishal Divakar, Rohit's brother, police said.

Subsequently, a case was registered in the matter at the Anti Narcotics Task Force police station under relevant provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, and the trio was arrested.
During investigation, police arrested the alleged receiver, Afroj Ali, from Roorkee in Uttarakhand on September 15.
The sixth accused, Gaurav, was arrested from Ghaziabad on November 10, with police seizing ₹36,000 of suspected drug money and a Mahindra Thar allegedly purchased with proceeds of narcotics trade.

items.title: Public Road Blocked For Birthday Celebration: What The Law Says [Video]
points: Most of us have faced the same situation near our homes where we have tried to cross a road.
Recently, a video has gone viral online which explains the step-by-step process of how to remove such blockades by people who think that they can use a public road for their private events.
The video explaining how a private event road blockage can be cleared has been shared on Instagram by Law With Arbaz on their page.
The influencer mentions that if anyone faces any similar issue, they can immediately call 112, which is the official police complaint number, and then ask them to come to the location.
Now, coming to the legal aspect, blocking a public road without the necessary permission is grounds for action under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023.
One of the most relevant provisions is Section 285.
Under this section, anyone responsible for creating such an obstruction can face a fine of up to Rs 5,000.

The test mule appears to be running 17-inch wheels, while higher variants could get larger 18-inch units.

items.title: Row Over Order To Shut Meat Shops In West Bengal's Rampurhat For Chhath Puja
points: A municipal body of a city in West Bengal's Birbhum has told meat shop owners to remain closed today and tomorrow on the occasion of Chhath Puja.
The order by the civic body in Rampurhat, 200 km from Kolkata, has sparked a political row.
In the order sent to all meat shop owners, Rampurhat civic body Chairman Soumen Bhakat said meat shops must remain closed until 10 am on Sunday and Monday.
Now, questions are being raised over why meat shops should be ordered to close down for a festival like Chhath Puja.
On other religious occasions such as Kaushiki Amavasya and Kali Puja, meat shops have never been told to shut down, critics of the municipal body's order said.
Following discussions attended by administrative officials, police representatives and elected representatives, it was decided that the shops would remain closed until 10 am on November 15 and 16.
Suddenly, after the change of government, this letter to the meat shops for Chhath Puja surprised us very much.

items.title: PM Modi credits tribal welfare schemes for poverty reduction, announces ₹3,000 crore projects
points: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday said nearly 50 crore people had moved out of extreme poverty over the past 12-13 years and claimed that the country had become free from Naxalism and Maoist terror, describing the two developments as major…
Referring to a recent World Bank report, Modi said nearly 50 crore people had emerged from extreme poverty in the past 12-13 years.
More than four crore permanent houses had been built for poor families, while electricity had been provided to 18,000 villages that had remained unelectrified for decades, he said.

Under Ayushman Bharat, eligible families were provided with health coverage of up to ₹5 lakh, while more than 1.75 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs had been established across the country, including in remote tribal regions.
Modi also highlighted the government’s focus on more than 100 Aspirational Districts and over 500 Aspirational Blocks, many of which have sizeable tribal populations.

items.title: Kolkata man kills live-in partner's two dogs after she moves out, shares videos with her
points: A man was detained in Kolkata after he allegedly killed his live-in partner's two dogs after she moved out, police said.
The accused, identified as Sanjib Bhattacharya, allegedly shared videos with his partner showing how he killed the dogs.
According to police, the woman, who recently quit her job as a DJ, owed the man a few lakh rupees.
She had left her pets, including two dogs and some cats, at the house.
The couple lived in a flat in Bikramgarh, in the Jadavpur area.
Popular Bengali actor and animal activist Debolina Dutta, who rushed to the spot, said Bhattacharya had identified himself in a video in which he described how he killed the dogs.

“In a video clip, he is proudly saying that as his live-in partner, who allegedly owed him a few lakh rupees, quit and moved out of the house, he strangled one dog and smashed the head of another puppy,” Dutta told media persons.
Joydeep Thakur is a Special Correspondent based in Kolkata.

items.title: How to Stop Spam Calls and SMS on Jio, Airtel, Vi and BSNL
points: TRAI’s Do Not Call framework will not block out unwanted calls entirely, but simply reduce them Thanks to AI, there has been a rise in the number of scams, most of which are implemented through basic SMS messages and voice calls.
Not everyone will get a call from a scammer, but we all get unwanted calls from a number of businesses on a daily basis.
While these may not be annoying the first time, it can get tiring when you are bombarded with spam calls and SMS messages during work or even when you are relaxing.
Since 2007, the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has implemented the Do Not Call (DND) framework.
It is a nationwide system which covers all cellular service providers.
Users can simply send START 0 to the 1909 to register their number for a full DND service.
Alternatively, users from any operator can also call TRAI's DND helpline in 1909 and then follow the IVR instructions to register the same.

points: An 18-year-old woman was allegedly killed by her relative inside a clothing showroom's trial room in west Delhi, where she worked, on Saturday night, police said on Sunday.
The incident near Moti Nagar Metro station came to light when the showroom staff found the body around 9pm, as they were getting ready to close for the day.
They immediately alerted the police, who rushed to the spot.

It appears that the woman and her sister's brother-in-law were in a dispute for three months, the police said.

items.title: FPIs infuse ₹84,290 cr into equities in first half of November
points: Foreign investors made a strong comeback to Indian equities in the first fortnight of November, pumping in ₹84,290 crore after two consecutive months of net outflows, amid a global AI sell-off, falling crude prices and attractive large-cap valuations.
